summary: The vault's only backup and its only migration path: a fully encrypted local file carrying every record and the password credential's one wrapper, and a replace-only import that re-keys the vault under a fresh DEK.

read.role: the per-record validator import reuses and the migration chain it shares
the profile the import replaces, and the one sanctioned way the main currency changes

sections: Where it lives: inside the vault
read.role: the second timeline the file must carry, and why version resetting to 1 rules out a version-based tiebreak
the round-trip assertion that the chart and both totals come back identical

both routes are vault routes, and GET /api/export is the one GET that requires the header. Configuration names the export limit's variable, and Database the attempts table its rows live in and their pruning
the progress, dialog and file-input conventions both screens use, and the phone-width sizes
where both screens are reached from, and the delete dialog that offers export first

exportEndpoint.value: GET /api/export returning a JSON file with Content-Disposition: attachment

exportFilename.value: solvent-vault-<YYYY-MM-DD>.json. The name carries no user identifier, for the same reason the contents carry none. Two vaults exported on one day collide in a downloads folder and the browser's own numbering is the answer to that

exportRequiresTheCsrfHeader.value: despite being a GET, so it is not reachable by navigation. The client fetches it and saves the response through a blob URL rather than pointing an anchor at it, and following the URL directly is a Forbidden

fileShape.value: { format: 'solvent-vault', formatVersion, exportedAt, salt, kdf, wrappedDek, dekNonce, records: [{ recordId, recordType, accountId, schemaVersion, version, nonce, ciphertext }] }

kdfEnvelopeInFile.value: { alg: 'argon2id', v: 19, m: 65536, t: 3, p: 1 }, which is Argon2id at 64 MiB, 3 iterations, parallelism 1

formatVersion.value: 1 is the current shape and there is nothing below it. A newer formatVersion is rejected with a clear message rather than guessed at, and an older one is migrated client-side after decryption and before re-encrypting, reusing the same per-type migration chain the client applies lazily on read

bothTimelines.value: quantities and prices are both ordinary vault records and both ride in the same records array, with no format change and no second section. A file missing the price entries would restore a vault whose whole history reprices itself

exactlyOneWrapper.value: the file carries exactly one wrapper, the password credential's. Not a list, and never a wrapper belonging to another method, because a wrapper bound to an authenticator does not travel and its credential id in a file would be a device correlator sitting in a backup

noUserIdentifier.value: the file carries no user identifier. A record's AAD is built from the record's own fields, so the ciphertext authenticates without knowing who exported it, which is also why the file is portable between accounts

sensitivityWarning.value: the export screen must state, in plain language and before the download starts, that this file is exactly as sensitive as the password, and that losing the password makes the file permanently unreadable

importIsReplaceOnly.value: import replaces the vault entirely and there is no merge. If the target vault holds records beyond its profile, the user must type ERASE against a dialog stating exactly how many records will be destroyed. A vault holding only its profile counts as empty: the review says nothing will be deleted and no ERASE is asked for

reKeyStep.value: records are decrypted with DEK_file and re-encrypted client-side under a freshly generated random 256-bit DEK_new with a fresh nonce, version resets to 1, and the AAD is rebuilt for that version. DEK_new is wrapped under the current session's Master Key, so the user's existing login password keeps working

reKeyReason.value: a verbatim restore would leave two accounts holding the same DEK, so a malicious or compromised server could inject the exporter's later records into the importer's vault, where they would decrypt cleanly. Re-keying makes the injection fail at the cryptography rather than at a check

importEndpoint.value: POST /api/import with the new wrapped DEK and the re-encrypted records. In one transaction the server deletes every record belonging to the session user, replaces the wrapper on their password credential, inserts the new set, and invalidates every other session for the user while keeping the importing one

everyWrapperRewritten.value: import is the one flow that changes the DEK, so every credential the vault holds must end the transaction wrapping DEK_new, and any method the importing session cannot re-wrap is deleted in that same transaction rather than left behind. A stale wrapper is worse than a missing one

credentialSurvivesImport.value: salt, KDF envelope and Auth Key are untouched by an import. The password does not change and the DEK does

profileIsReplacedToo.value: the main currency, dimensions and idle-lock setting all become the file's. The import review step names the change when the file's main currency differs from the current one

serverValidation.value: strict server-side validation before any write: total payload size cap, per-record ciphertext size cap, record count cap, known recordType values, well-formed UUIDs, base64 decodes cleanly, accountId present exactly for snapshot records and null for every other type and never the empty string, and referencing an account in the same import

sharedValidator.value: every record goes through the same per-record validator as PUT /api/records, field-consistency check included, and that validator also enforces version 1 on every imported record rather than trusting the client to have reset it. A record at any other version is a Bad Request for the whole payload

principalIdFromSession.value: the server assigns principal_id from the session on every imported record and never reads an account id from the uploaded payload

oneTransaction.value: the import is one transaction, and a failure at any point leaves the existing vault exactly as it was, never half-erased

otherSessionsInvalidated.value: every other session is invalidated in the same transaction, because a second session still holding DEK_old could create a record at version 1 that stores ciphertext under a key no longer in the envelope

exportRateLimit.value: default 5 per hour per user, operator config, variable EXPORTS_PER_USER_HOUR. It is a full vault read

exportRateLimitRows.value: one request row in the bucket export:<principal id> per export let through, deleted once older than 60 minutes. A refused request writes no row, in this limiter as in every other, so the limit lifts an hour after the oldest export it let through, however often the client retried

abortConditions.value: a wrong password for the file aborts at the DEK unwrap with nothing uploaded. One record failing to decrypt aborts the entire import and reports which record. An oversized file is rejected client-side by size before parse and server-side before write. A file with no profile record is refused before anything is decrypted, because it would restore a vault with no main currency

exportByNavigation.condition: a plain top-level navigation to GET /api/export with a valid session cookie present (spec/features/export-import.md#acceptance-criteria)

administratorSession.condition: both routes are on the vault surface (spec/features/export-import.md#rules)

payloadRejected.condition: an unknown recordType, a record at a version other than 1, a snapshot whose accountId names no account in the same payload, a principalId field at the top level or on a record, or any field-consistency failure. The whole payload is rejected and neither vault changes (spec/features/export-import.md#rules, spec/features/record-api.md#rules)

overSizeOrCountCap.condition: over the payload size cap, the per-record ciphertext cap or the record count cap (spec/architecture.md#storage-data-handling)

overExportRateLimit.condition: and no attempts row is written (spec/features/export-import.md#acceptance-criteria)

fixtures: a populated vault holding accounts, snapshots, rate entries and a profile, with its chart and both pricing-mode totals captured before the round trip
a record taken from the source vault after the export, for direct insertion into the destination's rows
a file with one record's ciphertext altered by a single byte
a second seeded vault owner's export file, for the vault-transfer case
a checked-in fixture file at formatVersion 1, kept past the point where the format advances to 2
a second live session for the importing user, holding DEK_old, attempting a create after the import commits
a hand-built POST /api/import carrying a principalId field naming another user, a record at version 2, a snapshot whose accountId names no account in the payload, and an unknown recordType
a fault injected mid-import, for the leave-the-original-vault-intact assertion
a vault holding only its profile, for the valid file carrying that one record and for the review into a vault that counts as empty
a stubbed clock and the attempts table readable row for row, for the refused-export-writes-no-row and lifts-an-hour-after-the-oldest assertions
focus: the re-key must be asserted directly: after an import the stored wrapped DEK must unwrap to a key that is not the file's DEK_file. A verbatim restore passes every other criterion in the list, which is exactly why this one has to be written

the injection regression needs a record taken from the source vault after the export and inserted straight into the destination's rows, which must fail to decrypt. This passes only because the two vaults hold different DEKs, and no functional test reaches it

an import must replace only the wrapped_dek and dek_nonce and leave params and verifier byte-identical, compared field by field. Logging in afterwards with the unchanged password is necessary and not sufficient, because a rewritten envelope carrying the same password would also sign in

the second session must be shown to be invalidated and its post-import create must be shown never to reach the vault. Checking that its next read returns Unauthorized leaves the write path untested, and the write is the one that produces a permanently unreadable record

the round trip has to be asserted on the decrypted payloads of both timelines and on the redrawn chart and both pricing-mode totals. A file that drops the price entries restores a plausible vault and fails only here

the file must be scanned for known plaintext values, an account name, a note, a dimension label, a value, a rate, a symbol, a date and a currency, over the actual bytes rather than over the documented shape
GET /api/export must be shown to return Forbidden as a plain top-level navigation with a valid session cookie present. With the cookie absent the test passes for the wrong reason
a fixture file at formatVersion 1 must still import after the format advances, which only holds if the checked-in fixture is kept rather than regenerated

an export over the per-user limit must be shown to write no attempts row: retry repeatedly while over it, compare the table row for row, and show the limit lifting an hour after the oldest export it let through. A limiter that records each refused request extends the throttle with every retry and never lifts
the exported filename must be shown to carry no user identifier, asserted against the Content-Disposition header rather than against whatever the browser saved it as
